questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ 0x+y-3z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=-3,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-4z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x+2y-4z=3
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=3-2y+4z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2y+4z \\ y=y \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $y,z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3-2y+4z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 & 18\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 & 18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & -12 & 16 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 & 18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & -12 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 34\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y-6z=8 \\ 0x-y-12z=16 \\ 0x+0y+0z=34\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=34,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x+5y+0z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
-x+5y=3
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=5y-3.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5y-3 \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5y-3 \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
questions.problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=2 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-15{x}_{3}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for the system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & -15 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & -15 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & -15 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
